specification.problem: Implement a universal one- and two-qubit gate set on two exchange-coupled electron spins with constant non-diagonal exchange and small g-factor difference, using magnetic-field amplitude control (a few Gauss) and optimal control to find the evolution.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction: a standard two-spin Heisenberg-exchange Hamiltonian with a Zeeman term, a rotating-frame resonant drive on one spin, and a generic gate-fidelity cost for optimal control. The actual control fields, the non-diagonal exchange form, the suppression scheme via repeated single-spin rotations, the optimal-control algorithm and the numerical results are outside this scope.

symbols.meaning: magnetic field amplitude along z, controlled over a few Gauss
gate fidelity used as optimal-control objective

equations.label: Two-spin Hamiltonian
equations.description: Generic Heisenberg exchange between two electron spins with a Zeeman term in which the g-factors differ slightly, giving different resonance frequencies.
equations.justification: The abstract mentions constant exchange and a g-factor difference but gives no explicit Hamiltonian. The isotropic form is a placeholder and may differ from the paper's non-diagonal form.
assumptions: Static field plus control amplitude in B(t)

equations.label: Selective resonance condition
equations.description: Each spin has its own Larmor frequency, so a drive tuned to omega_k addresses spin k. The small difference Delta omega enables addressing.
equations.justification: Standard Zeeman resonance; consistent with the abstract's claim that a g-factor difference allows addressing qubits.
assumptions: Weak exchange relative to Zeeman splitting is not guaranteed

equations.label: Time evolution
equations.description: Time-ordered propagator generated by the controlled Hamiltonian.
equations.justification: Standard quantum dynamics for the evolution that the optimal control determines.

equations.label: Gate fidelity objective
equations.description: Phase-insensitive gate fidelity to be maximized over the control B(t).
equations.justification: The abstract says optimal control theory is used to find the evolution but does not state the cost functional. This is a common choice.
assumptions: Computational subspace is the full 4-dimensional space

steps.description: Define the two-spin Hamiltonian with constant exchange and a field B(t) acting on both spins with different g-factors.
Parametrize B(t) as piecewise constant with amplitude variations of a few Gauss, bringing spin 1 and then spin 2 into resonance.
Propagate the system under the control field to obtain U(T).
Optimize the control parameters to maximize fidelity with the target one- or two-qubit gate.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Classical optimization loop over the control amplitudes (algorithm unspecified in the abstract).
assumptions: Isotropic Heisenberg exchange is used in place of the paper's non-diagonal exchange
The cost functional is the trace fidelity
Suppression of exchange via repeated single-spin rotations is not modeled
missing_information: Exact form of the non-diagonal exchange Hamiltonian
Values of J, g_1, g_2 and field amplitudes
The suppression scheme via repeated single-spin rotations
The specific optimal control algorithm and parametrization
Target gate definitions and gate times
